Eri: What...? You can't go back to the <Earth Cradle>?
Sophia: That's right. Dr. Mitar Zapato's team will be handling the aftermath on their own.
Sophia: Looking back, the way he sent me off to the <Tesla Reich Institute> right after that...
Sophia: It was a ploy to cut me off from the Earth Cradle completely.
Jonathan: Mitar Zapato, huh... Rumor has it he's heading up something called the Tsentr Project.
Eri: The Tsentr Project?
Jonathan: Apparently it's a plan being run under Federation Army jurisdiction, but I don't know the details.
Jonathan: Most of its members seem to be from outside the <EOTI Institute> and the <DC>... I have no connections there.
Jonathan: So no information reaches us. They haven't poached anyone from us, either...
Jonathan: I doubt they have many people from <Mao Industries> or <Isurugi Heavy Industries>, current or former.
Eri: Is that so...
Jonathan: Anyone Dr. Anzai knew who might have been pulled into it?
Eri: No, no one.
Jonathan: Hmm... The blatant secrecy bothers me, but this was an official order from the top brass, wasn't it?
Sophia: Yes...
Jonathan: Then there's no way to look into it for now.
Eri: What on earth are they doing in the Earth Cradle...?
Sophia: ...Dr. Mitar Zapato may be after the Cradle's central computer, Magus, and the <Machine Cells>.
Jonathan: But both of those have stopped functioning, haven't they?
Sophia: ...Yes. Thanks to Major Sombold and everyone on the Kurogane.
Jonathan: I'll ask Major Gilliam about the Tsentr Project's activities when I get the chance.
Sophia: Please do.
Eri: Sophia... what will you do now?
Sophia: I'll go over the Earth Cradle data I have and keep reviewing Project Ark...
Sophia: I don't know what lies ahead, but there's another Cradle on the moon... I hope it'll be of some use.
Jonathan: In that case, you're welcome to keep staying here at the Tesla Institute.
Sophia: Are you sure?
Jonathan: In return, if I may, perhaps the two of us could have dinner sometime...
Eri: ...Director Kazahara.
Jonathan: Ahem. Anyway, please stay here until you've decided where to go next.
Sophia: Yes, thank you very much.
Eri: Say, Sophia. Only when you have time, but... could you help me with my work?
Sophia: Is it related to the <Chokijin>?
Eri: Yes. Since the <Inspector Incident> ended, they've been dormant, as you can see.
Eri: Partly at the wish of their pilots, Lieutenant Brooklyn Luckfield and Lieutenant Kusuha Mizuha...
Eri: We suspended the analysis to let RyuOhKi and KoOhKi rest, but something seems a little off.
Sophia: Off?
Eri: It's less like sleep and closer to suspended animation. They might never wake up at all...
Sophia: ...
Eri: So I plan to resume the analysis once Lieutenant Brooklyn and Lieutenant Kusuha give their consent.
Eri: It would really help if you could be my advisor on it...
Sophia: Of course. ...We were classmates at university, after all. I'll help you.
Eri: Thank you, Sophia.
Jonathan: I knew you two went to the same university, but your fields were different. Where did you meet?
Eri: We were both in the exploration club.
Jonathan: Exploration?
Sophia: Yes. We went to all sorts of caves and ruins.
Eri: We did survival training too, didn't we?
Sophia: Oh yes, that was rough. We got caught in the rain and ended up covered in mud.
Jonathan: (...So these two had that vitality even back then.)

Lamia: ...I have been awaiting you, Major.
Kai: Radha told me the situation. Sorry you had to come all the way to Aviano.
Lamia: Not at all. An incident like the one at Incirlik could occur again.
Kai: I can't take that kind of thing happening over and over. ...By the way, the Kai models?
Lamia: All three arrived at this base yesterday... They are undergoing startup settings in Hangar 23.
Lamia: Also, Orleans reports they have prepared-ed two F2W Beam Cannons... or so it seems that it is.
Kai: That's one short. Give them to the Cry Wolves, then.
Lamia: Are you sure?
Kai: My unit's the Double Buckler spec. I'll use the long arm I brought with me.
Lamia: Understood. Two pilots from the Cry Wolves have come to receive their units...
Lamia: Will you be taking your Kai model right away as well, Major?
Kai: Yeah. I want some time to buy souvenirs later.

Hugo: So this is the MP Gespenst Mk-II Kai...
Albero: A solid, practical upgrade. I like how sturdy it feels.
Hugo: For us, after flying Gespensts all this time, it looks easy to handle.
Albero: Yes. Judging by the spec notes, it shouldn't handle much differently.
Hugo: ...By the way, Captain. Am I really supposed to pilot this new model?
Albero: The aptitude review picked you and me as the Kai model pilots.
Hugo: But I'm...
Albero: Mao Industries apparently chose pilots with long and short combat time on purpose...
Albero: But I hear survivability and unit damage rates in actual combat were criteria too.
Hugo: So in my case... they rated how fast I can run away?
Albero: Don't sell yourself short. Mao Industries judged well. Have some confidence.
Hugo: But with Lieutenant Ethan and the others to think of...
Albero: ...Other units have plenty of people who are merely good at fighting.
Albero: But what the Cry Wolves demand is completing the mission and coming back alive from certain death.
Albero: Death may mean something to others, but to yourself it's meaningless. Your own death teaches you nothing.
Albero: Accomplish the mission, and cling to life. Those two must always be kept in balance.
Hugo: ...
Albero: You're still inexperienced and rough around the edges... but you have what it takes to keep that balance.
Hugo: Would you say the same of Foglia, sir?
Albero: ...Yes. But he tends to fixate on his own results.
Hugo: ...Captain, why did you bring him into the Cry Wolves?
Albero: To keep my own balance. On the battlefield, blood ties are often a liability...
Albero: The question is whether we can both overcome that and be nothing but soldiers.
Albero: Call it discipline. He... and I are both still unfinished.
Hugo: But... someone like you, Captain?
Albero: Don't overrate me. I did fail in the White Star operation, after all.
Hugo: I don't believe your judgment back then was wrong, sir.
Hugo: If anything, the requests from Dr. Zapato and Dr. Wang were the problem...
Albero: That's enough, Hugo. It's not our job to probe their true intentions.
Hugo: ...Yes, sir.
Kai: ...It's been a while, Major Albero Est.
Albero: Kai... Kai Kitamura, is it?
Kai: Not since we met during the DC War.
Albero: ...Yes.
Albero: (Face to face, at least.)
Lamia: ...
Lamia: (Cry Wolves captain, Albero Est. ...So his position is the same on "this side" too.)
Albero: And she is?
Kai: My subordinate.
Albero: Then she's a member of the <Tactical Instructor Corps>.
Lamia: Sir. I'm Second Lieutenant Lamia Loveless, that I am-ish. ...Pray hear my humble introduction, eh?
Albero: Hm? What did you just say?
Lamia: (Damn... The Major never minds it, so I let my guard down...!)
Kai: It's a dialect, Major. ...Lamia Loveless. She's a skilled pilot.
Albero: Forgive me, I was just a little surprised. Let me introduce my subordinate as well.
Hugo: Warrant Officer Hugo Medio, sir.
Kai: So you're the pilot of Kai-type Unit 3.
Hugo: Yes, sir. It's an honor to meet a member of the legendary original Instructor Corps, Major Kai Kitamura.
Kai: Cut it out. I'm not nearly as intense as the rest of that bunch.
Hugo: (R-really...?)
Kai: I helped plan the Kai-type too. It's a machine by Gespenst pilots, for Gespenst pilots. Treat it well.
Hugo: Understood.
Albero: By the way, Major Kai. We'd like to finish our fitting as soon as possible.
Albero: To break them in, I'd like to run a light mock battle with your side... How about it?
Kai: Gladly. Let's start preparing right away.
Lamia: Reached the exercise area.
Kai: Condition green. The servos are turning nicely, and the sole grip's in great shape.
Lamia: From where I'm sitting, the limbs seem to move more naturally...
Kai: Yeah, the range of motion's wider now.
Lamia: And has the frame's rigidity gone and gotten improved-ified as well-ish?
Kai: Which does make me a bit worried about the load on the servomotors...
Kai: It's built for small production runs, so we can't be picky. We never meant to tune it to extremes anyway.
Lamia: I see... So its characteristics will come from the options mounted on each hardpoint?
Kai: Eventually. And that's exactly why we need case studies from other units.
Albero: Hmm... Nothing feels off. It handles like an extension of the normal type. ...How's yours, Hugo?
Hugo: It's nimbler than I expected, and it sits lower than the mass-produced Hückebein, so it feels stable...
Hugo: Personally, I think it's a good machine.
Albero: But pilots used to the Hückebein's lightness will find it hard to handle.
Albero: Mastering this one takes skill... It's a machine for aces.
Hugo: (An ace, huh... Can I ever become a pilot like the Captain or Major Kai?)
Albero: Recheck your joint range of motion. We're facing the Instructor Corps... and one's a Super Robot.
Albero: Botch this, and our brand-new units get shipped back to the factory. ...Don't forget our mission.
Hugo: Yes, sir...
Hugo: (So this is the perfect chance to gather data up close, not from a distance like before.)
Hugo: (But look who we're up against. If I don't give it everything, I'll get taken down.)
Lamia: (Hmm... Albero Est is a given, but his subordinate moves well too.)
Lamia: Warrant Officer Hugo Medio... He seems quite skilled.
Kai: Yeah... Major Albero seems to have trained him well.
Lamia: ...Speaking of Major Albero.
Kai: What is it?
Lamia: Major Kai and Major Albero... since when did you two become such buddy-wuddies-ish?
Kai: I met him after the old Instructor Corps disbanded. We worked together on motion data projects a few times.
Lamia: (I see, so that's why...)
Kai: The <TC-OS> motion data we built was mostly for solo operation or two-unit coordination.
Kai: Of course, we made squad-level data too, but the Corps disbanded partway through.
Kai: After that, the PTX Team, where Irm used to be...
Kai: ...and several units, including Major Albero's Cry Wolves, took it over and refined the data.
Lamia: I see.
Albero: Hm? What's this...?
Hugo: What is it, Captain?
Albero: Switch to P-mode.
Hugo: Sir.
Albero: Hugo, we've received word that Foglia's team is under attack by hostile attack craft.
Hugo: !
Albero: The transport they were escorting made a forced landing, and they seem to be struggling.
Albero: If I push it, I can just barely reach the combat zone. You stay here.
Hugo: No, sir. I'm going too.
Albero: It's dangerous to go into combat before the break-in period is complete.
Hugo: I know it's a little reckless, sir. But I'll master this Kai model. You'll see.
Albero: ...Very well.
Albero: Major Kai, I'll have to call off the mock battle. Something urgent has come up.
Kai: Something urgent?
Albero: My subordinates are engaging hostile attack craft. We're heading out to assist them now.
Kai: Then we'll come with you. There's your machine to think of, too. More hands should help.
Albero: (...I can't let this man learn about our ties to the Tsentr Project.)
Albero: (But securing the cargo takes priority over keeping secrets...)
Albero: Understood. I'm counting on you.
Kai: Sir.
Foglia: (Tch, splitting up the formation backfired...!)
Foglia: (I got the No. 2 and No. 3 transports away, but to think they'd throw that much at us...)
Foglia: (Those guys must know what the No. 1 transport is carrying. There's no other explanation...)
Foglia: What?! What's this?!
Albero: Wolf 9, are you all right?
Foglia: Captain!
Albero: We'll draw the enemy's attention. You focus on defending the transport.
Foglia: Just focus on that...?!
Albero: Repeat your orders, Wolf 9.
Foglia: Roger...! Wolf 9 defending the transport.
Albero: ...Wolf 8, cover Wolf 9.
Hugo: Roger. ...Foglia, hold out till I get there.
Foglia: ...Yeah.
Foglia: (So the old man gave Hugo a new model...)
Hugo: Foglia...
Foglia: Nothing. More to the point, those are some Superior reinforcements you brought along.
Hugo: It's the Tactical Instructor Corps. Things just worked out so they're helping us.
Foglia: (So this time they get to watch the show fair and square, huh?)
Foglia: (But now I really can't let anyone else steal the spotlight.)
Lamia: There seems to be no doubt the enemy units are Neue DC remnants.
Kai: But I doubt they can spare that much force for a place like this right now.
Lamia: You mean they have another backer?
Kai: That's the reasonable assumption.
Kai: (The new patron Donna mentioned, or else...)
Lamia: Whatever the case, that transport's cargo must be just chock-full of treasure-y goodies, I'd be supposing.
Kai: Yeah. And treasure, to DC remnants, would mean...
Albero: Wolf 1 to Ghost 1. I'll take the forward position. I'm counting on your support.
Kai: Roger.

Kai: The motion data transplant is flawless... and the response is excellent.
Kai: The folks at Orleans did fine work!
Lamia: (Neue DC... The Shadow Mirror unit is gone, yet these people still haven't disappeared.)
Lamia: (...No. Shadow Mirror still has me. Perhaps this too is... fate.)
Hugo: Never thought I'd be breaking it in during actual combat...!
Hugo: But I'm the one who asked for this. I'll pull it off!
Albero: (To think the transport would be attacked... Has the information leaked outside the military?)
Albero: (If so, who's behind it?)
Hugo: Foglia! Don't leave the transport!
Foglia: I'm just adapting to the situation! Back me up!
Hugo: Foglia!
Foglia: (Sorry, Hugo. I've got something to prove to the old man.)
Albero: ...
Lamia: All enemy units shot down. Area clear.
Kai: The transport... looks like it made it through somehow.
Albero: Thank you for your support. Leave the rest to us and return to base.
Kai: ...Major Albero, what's aboard that transport?
Albero: We were only ordered to escort it. I don't know what's inside.
Kai: Then where did the transport come from?
Albero: That's classified. I can't tell you.
Lamia: ...
Kai: ...
Kai: ...Understood. Lamia, can you hold on to what we've got?
Lamia: Yes. ...But are you sure about this?
Kai: We're heading back.
Lamia: ...Roger.
Albero: ...
Hugo: Foglia, are you okay?
Foglia: Yeah...
Hugo: Tell me. What did you bring from the Earth Cradle?
Foglia: I don't know either. One of Mitar's men just told me to protect the transport carrying the Container.
Hugo: ...
Foglia: Probably something nasty again. Bad enough for Neue DC remnants to come after it.
Hugo: (Does the captain know what's in the Container...?)
Albero: ...Wolf 9. Why did you disobey my orders?
Foglia: ...!
Albero: I told you to focus on guarding the transport. Why did you leave it?
Foglia: It was the result of adapting my judgment to the situation, sir.
Albero: Weren't you just too eager for glory?
Foglia: ...No, sir.
Albero: If you pull something like that again, I'll take you off the mission. Understood?
Foglia: ...Understood, Captain.

Lamia: Major Kai, our ride from Izu arrives in two hours.
Kai: Right. The Angelg and the Gespenst are ready to be loaded.
Kai: Let's take a breather until the transport gets here.
Lamia: Yes-sir-ee~
Kai: By the way... have you found out where the Cry Wolves went?
Lamia: Ahem... No, it seems Aviano hasn't been contacted.
Kai: Where are they stationed right now?
Lamia: That's unknown as well. The Cry Wolves' missions are classified at the Double-A level.
Kai: For a special ops PT unit, that's to be expected... but something about it bugs me.
Lamia: Shadow Mirror--over on the 'other side,' mind you--used its position in the Federation Army to scheme.
Lamia: And in the end... they rebelled.
Kai: Knowing Major Albero, I can't see the Cry Wolves walking the same path as Shadow Mirror.
Lamia: (Right... On the 'other side,' the Cry Wolves became Shadow Mirror's enemy.)
Lamia: (They were never a unit with political ideals. That likely holds true on 'this side' as well...)
Kai: ...And I'm also curious about the ones who attacked the transport.
Lamia: Shall I dig a little deeper? It's possible that...
Kai: No, not now. Poke carelessly at a Double-A secret, and we could get badly burned.
Kai: Besides, there's the next-gen mainline trial. We can't stay out of that one either.
Lamia: Looks like we'll be coming back here again.
Kai: Probably. The work's piling up.
Lamia: I can handle it in low-load normal mode. I don't mind at all.
Kai: Even so, I've been working you too hard. You need a break once in a while.
Lamia: No, the W Series artificial humans needs way less sleep than you Major-dears, kinda sorta, doesn't we-ish?
Kai: Don't push yourself. See? You're tripping over your words.
Lamia: ...You usually ignore it, so kindly be ignoring it now too, dammit-please.
Aqua: U-um, excuse me-ness! Are you being Major Kai Kitamura of the Tactical Instructor Corps, sirs!?
Kai: Hm? Wh-What is it?
Lamia: That, Major, is what tripping over your words looks like.
Aqua: Ah, wh-what am I saying!?
Kai: And you are?
Aqua: Y-Yes, sir! I'm Aqua Centrum, PT pilot candidate!
Kai: Oh?
Aqua: It's a great honor to meet you, Major. And, um... if it's all right with you...
Kai: ?
Aqua: C-Could I please have your autograph!?
Kai: M-My autograph...? Hmm, that's not really my style...
Aqua: P-Please, I'm begging you! You and the Instructor Corps are what all us candidates look up to!
Kai: ...All right, all right. So, what should I sign?
Aqua: Huh? Oh! Um, let's see...
Aqua: (Oh no! I never thought I'd run into him here...)
Lamia: Let's see... I can offer this memo pad, if that will do.
Aqua: Y-Yes. Thank you very much...
Aqua: (Wow... She's so beautiful... Like a doll...)
Aqua: Um, are you with the Instructor Corps too...? Or wait, are you Major Kai's wife...?
Kai: Pfft! H-Hey! How did you come up with that!?
Lamia: Sadly, I am merely his subordinate. Lieutenant Lamia Loveless, Instructor Corps.
Aqua: (Corps WAVEs are odd. She wears that sexy getup like it's nothing... I could never pull that off...)
Aqua: I-If possible, could I have your autograph too, Lieutenant...?
Lamia: Understood. ......................There. Will this do?
Aqua: Y-Yes! ...Whoa, that's huge!
Lamia: Now then, Major...
Kai: Whew. Never thought a young girl would want my autograph... Whoa, that's huge! Your signature!
Kai: There's no room left. ...Oh well, I'll squeeze it in around here... K-a-i K-i-t-a-m-u-r-a.
Aqua: Th-Thank you so much! I'll treasure it forever!
Kai: Keep up with your training and become a good pilot.
Aqua: Yes, sir! Excuse me, then!
Kai: Sheesh. Full of energy, that one.
Lamia: ...A rookie, huh. A concept the W Series lack. But oddly, watching her doesn't feel bad...
Kai: Heh, she tickled your maternal instinct, I take it? You look like a mother watching over her child, Lamia.
Lamia: (A mother...? Me...?)
Kai: Now then... let's go buy some souvenirs while we can.
Announcement: Major Kai Kitamura, Tactical Instructor Corps, to General Mauro Gatt's office, Level 4. Repeat...
Kai: ...Sigh. There goes my free time.
Aviano Base - Interior
Mauro: Lieutenants Lamia Loveless and Latune Subbota, Sergeants Arado Balanga and Seolla Schweizer... these four...
Mauro: ...are to take part in the next-gen mainline trial to be held here at Aviano.
Kai: Sir. Will they be running evaluation tests on the trial units?
Mauro: You'll be notified of mission details and dates later.
Kai: Understood.
Mauro: ...Judging by the files, they're still young. In fact, three of them are children.
Mauro: It's not that I doubt their ability data, but... they'll be all right, won't they?
Kai: They survived hell against the Inspectors, Shadow Mirror and the Einst. That's why they're in the Corps.
Mauro: Even so, compared to the old Instructor Corps members... I don't know.
Kai: I suppose they can't help lacking an imposing look.
Mauro: That's not what I meant.
Kai: (You're still worried about appearances, though.)
Kai: General... I chose them for their potential.
Mauro: Very well. This trial holds a key place in the <Aegis Plan>. Make sure your subordinates understand that.
Kai: Sir. ...By the way, I'm not to take part in the trial myself?
Mauro: No. I'd rather not owe Kenneth any more favors.
Kai: (So he knows that octopus-headed old man...)
Mauro: Any other questions?
Kai: One, sir. Will any Tsentr Project units be taking part in the trial?
Mauro: The Tsentr Project...? I've heard the name, but not the details. In any case, it's submitting no units.
Kai: Understood.
Kai: (Donna's Wendigo was only a prototype...)
Kai: (So the Tsentr Project's machines aren't ready to be shown in public yet...)

Eric: Oho, from the Earth Cradle, eh?
Mitar: All that patient searching paid off.
Eric: But a good long while has passed since then. Can it even be regenerated, I wonder?
Mitar: We'll use Lazmnanium. Whether it'll take, we won't know until we try...
Mitar: If the rejection is severe, we freeze it for now and wait for that man to wake up.
Eric: Another sleeping prince... No, a sleeping lizard, more like. Will he even do as we say?
Mitar: We've played the game of feeling each other out before. We'll use him as far as he's useful.
Eric: My, my, we've plenty of difficult guests, don't we? Including this... "Head."
Mitar: But... if we can control it, this will become a biological weapon without equal.
Eric: And if we fail, we won't get off lightly.
Mitar: We'll run tests with a Flatfish that has its cells incorporated.
Eric: Hmmm... I don't think much of using the Einst as weapons, you know.
Eric: Its appearance has been changing, perhaps from the Lazmnanium we put into it...
Eric: And it's got the face of something that won't listen to a word you say.
Mitar: ...Don't judge it by its face.
Eric: Whatever the case, I don't care for this sort of thing.
Mitar: You'll have to accept it, Dr. Wang. Depending on how things go, it may become our trump card...
Mitar: This Einst... No, this "Jetzt."

Izu Base - Interior
Kai: ...I'm back.
Seolla: Welcome back, Major Kai. You too, Lieutenant Lamia.
Lamia: Yes. Has anything changed here?
Latune: No, there haven't been any particular problems.
Arado: So how was the business trip? Get to eat anything good?
Kai: I did more drinking than eating, if anything... But yeah, a little.
Arado: You went to Incirlik in Turkey, right? So did you have real, authentic Toruko rice?
Kai: That dish didn't come from Turkey. It comes from Nagasaki, in Japan.
Arado: Huh? Seriously?
Seolla: Arado, what's Toruko rice?
Arado: It's pilaf and spaghetti with a pork cutlet on top, and then demi-glace sauce poured over all of it.
Seolla: Th-That sounds like a lot of calories...
Latune: Sounds exactly like the kind of thing Arado would love.
Arado: You gotta eat stuff like that too, or you'll never grow up big!
Radha: ...Major, what about souvenirs for your wife and daughter?
Kai: In the end, I never had time to go buy any.
Radha: I thought as much, so I had some sent over myself.
Kai: Thanks again. Also, send the electronic documents that piled up while I was away to my terminal.
